intervention_dose: 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
indication: HER2-expressing locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors (seven cohorts; bladder cohort n=41), excluding breast, gastric, colorectal and NSCLC
population_detail: HER2 IHC 3+ or 2+ by local or central testing, progression after >=1 systemic therapy or no satisfactory alternative; ECOG 0-1. Bladder cohort was metastatic or advanced urothelial carcinoma of renal pelvis, ureter, bladder or urethra. Prior HER2-directed therapy was permitted.
median_dor_or_pfs: all-cohort mDOR 11.3 mo, mPFS 6.9 mo; central IHC 3+ mDOR 22.1 mo, mPFS 11.9 mo

outcomes.name: DoR
outcomes.notes: all patients; 22.1 mo in central IHC 3+

outcomes.name: PFS
outcomes.notes: all patients; 11.9 mo in central IHC 3+

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: all patients, 66% maturity; 21.1 mo in central IHC 3+

safety_summary: Grade >=3 drug-related AEs in 40.8%; drug-related deaths 1.5%. Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis in 10.5% (three fatal). Nausea was the single most common drug-related AE at 55.1%.
notes: The trial the current T-DXd course rests on; per-term AE rates and the bladder-cohort breakdown were read from PMC full text (PMC10730032) because ClinicalTrials.gov posts no results for NCT04482309. Bladder IHC 3+ rests on 16 patients, so the tier-matched estimate for this patient is wide, and the whole argument depends on whether the current tumor is still 3+ rather than on the 2023-2025 stains.

intervention_dose: 5.4-8.0 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks across nine monotherapy studies
indication: HER2-positive, HER2-low or HER2-mutant solid tumors (breast 44.3%, gastric 25.6%, lung 17.7%, colorectal 9.3%)
population_detail: Median 4 prior lines; median treatment duration 5.8 months. Independent adjudication committee re-reviewed all investigator-reported ILD events.
design: Pooled safety analysis of nine phase 1-2 monotherapy studies

outcomes.name: TTP
outcomes.notes: median time to first ILD event; 87.0% occurred within 12 months

safety_summary: Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis in 15.4%, fatal in 2.2%; 77.4% of events were grade 1-2 and 87% occurred within the first 12 months. Pre-existing lung comorbidity, oxygen saturation <95%, dose >6.4 mg/kg and renal impairment were among the baseline risk factors identified.

toxicities.notes: 77.4% of the adjudicated ILD events were grade 1 or 2; the paper reports the proportion of events, not a population rate

notes: The risk-factor list includes pre-existing lung comorbidity, which is precisely what the disputed 2026-03 chest CT read would establish if it is correct. Adjudicated onset preceded the investigator-recognised onset in 53.2% of events by a median of 43 days, so baseline imaging ambiguity has a direct cost in this case.

intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) — retreatment after grade 1 ILD
intervention_dose: 5.4-8.0 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks, resumed after radiographic resolution
indication: HER2-positive, HER2-low or HER2-mutant solid tumors
population_detail: Patients who recovered from a first investigator-graded grade 1, adjudication-confirmed drug-related ILD event and were then retreated (45 of 193 eligible).
design: Pooled analysis of nine clinical trials
median_dor_or_pfs: median retreatment duration 85 days (range 1-848); 17.8% retreated for >=1 year

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: grade 1 first ILD event across the pooled population (193/2145)

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: ILD recurrence among retreated patients (15/45); all grade 1-2

outcomes.name: TTP
outcomes.notes: median time from retreatment to ILD recurrence

outcomes.name: discontinuation_rate
outcomes.notes: retreatment stopped for ILD recurrence; 33.3% stopped for progression

safety_summary: One-third of retreated patients had a second ILD event, all grade 1-2 with no grade >=3 or fatal recurrence; 60% of recurrences recovered with or without sequelae.

toxicities.notes: grade 1 n=6, grade 2 n=9; no grade >=3 events

notes: Directly relevant if the 2026-03 CT read is confirmed and T-DXd is held: resuming after a resolved grade 1 event carried no fatal recurrence in this series. Only 45 patients were retreated and they were selected by their treating physicians, so the recurrence rate is a floor rather than an unbiased estimate.

intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) — gastrointestinal and hematologic AE pooled analysis
intervention_dose: 5.4 or 6.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
indication: Metastatic breast, gastric or lung cancer with varying HER2 expression or HER2 mutation
population_detail: Pooled from DS8201-A-J101, DESTINY-Breast01/02/03/04, DESTINY-Lung01/02 and DESTINY-Gastric01/02. Antiemetic analysis limited to before the 2020 protocol change that recommended prophylaxis.
design: Pooled safety analysis of nine phase 1-3 trials
safety_summary: Nausea affected roughly three-quarters of patients at the 5.4 mg/kg dose and fatigue 56.5%; TEAEs forced dose reduction in 22.6%, interruption in 42.8% and discontinuation in 17.7%.
notes: Quantifies the toxicity that is currently dose-limiting for this patient: severe nausea after dose 2 sits at the severe end of a very common event, and dose reduction rather than discontinuation is the modal response in the trials. Rates are pooled across breast, gastric and lung studies, not urothelial.

intervention_dose: 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
indication: HER2-low metastatic breast cancer (IHC 1+, or IHC 2+ with negative ISH) after one or two prior chemotherapy lines
population_detail: 88.7% hormone receptor-positive; primary endpoint PFS in the hormone receptor-positive cohort.
safety_summary: Grade >=3 AEs in 52.6% versus 67.4% with chemotherapy; adjudicated drug-related ILD in 12.1%, grade 5 in 0.8%.
notes: The whole basis for treating a HER2-low result as actionable is breast cancer, not urothelial. If the 2026-08 re-stain returns 1+ or 2+/ISH-negative, T-DXd in this patient becomes off-label extrapolation from this trial rather than tumor-agnostic on-label use, which requires IHC 3+.

intervention_dose: 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks
indication: Hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer with HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-negative) or HER2-ultralow (IHC 0 with membrane staining) expression, after >=1 endocrine-based line and no prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease
population_detail: 713 HER2-low and 153 HER2-ultralow patients; primary endpoint PFS by BICR in the HER2-low group.
outcome: median PFS by BICR, HER2-low population
safety_summary: Grade >=3 AEs in 52.8% versus 44.4% with chemotherapy; adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis in 11.3% (49 patients) including three grade 5 events, against one grade 2 event in the chemotherapy arm.
notes: Extends the HER2-low argument down to ultralow staining, again only in breast cancer and only against chemotherapy in a chemotherapy-naive metastatic population. Overall survival was immature at this analysis, so the ultralow signal rests on PFS alone.

intervention_dose: 2 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks
indication: HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or 2+) locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
population_detail: Pooled RC48-C005 and RC48-C009; all patients had progressed on >=1 prior systemic chemotherapy line. Subgroups included liver metastases and prior anti-PD-1/L1 exposure.
design: Pooled analysis of two single-arm phase 2 studies
outcome: confirmed ORR by blinded independent review
safety_summary: Peripheral sensory neuropathy was the most common treatment-related AE at 68.2% all-grade and 18.7% grade >=3; grade >=3 TRAEs overall 54.2%.
notes: The highest response rate of any HER2-directed agent in urothelial carcinoma, but the payload is MMAE and two-thirds of patients developed sensory neuropathy, which collides with this patient's established CIPN. Chinese-registration data; the drug has no US approval and the registered trials exclude prior HER2-directed therapy.

intervention_dose: disitamab vedotin 2.0 mg/kg with toripalimab 3.0 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks (RP2D)
indication: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma, HER2-unselected
population_detail: 61% treatment-naive; the rest chemo-refractory. Enrollment was not gated on HER2 expression.
design: Open-label phase 1b/2 dose escalation and expansion (RC48-C014)
safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 51.2%; peripheral sensory neuropathy 63.4% all-grade; one treatment-related death from pneumonitis.
notes: Shows a HER2 ADC working in urothelial carcinoma without an expression gate, which is the argument that would survive a downgraded re-stain. Neuropathy again reached 63.4% and one patient died of pneumonitis, so both of this case's active toxicity constraints apply.

intervention_dose: 20 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks (recommended part-2 dose)
indication: Locally advanced or metastatic HER2-expressing or HER2-amplified solid tumors of any type after all approved therapies
population_detail: Part 2 enrolled biliary tract (n=22), colorectal (n=28) and other HER2-expressing/amplified cancers excluding breast and gastroesophageal (n=36).
design: First-in-human phase 1 dose escalation and expansion (NCT02892123)

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: six grade 3 treatment-related events in four of 132 patients, reported as 3%

safety_summary: Diarrhoea (43-52%) and infusion reactions (34-43%) dominated and were almost all grade 1-2; six grade 3 treatment-related events occurred in four of 132 patients and there were no treatment-related deaths.

toxicities.notes: part 2; all grade 1-2 except one patient

notes: The non-ADC HER2 route: no cytotoxic payload, so neither the neuropathy nor the ILD constraint applies, at the cost of a lower and less durable response signal outside biliary tract cancer. The registered pan-tumor cohort now bars prior HER2-directed therapy, which current T-DXd triggers.

intervention_dose: per FDA label for each agent
indication: HER2-amplified and/or overexpressed and/or mutated solid tumors, tissue-agnostic cohort
population_detail: 263 patients with HER2 amplification and/or overexpression; 83 with HER2 mutation alone. Activity was stratified by KRAS status and by HER2 IHC tier.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: two of the five complete responses were urothelial

safety_summary: Diarrhoea (36.1%), fatigue (29.4%) and nausea (22.4%) led the non-serious events on the trastuzumab plus pertuzumab arm; serious events were infrequent and scattered, none above 1.7%.

toxicities.notes: non-serious AE tab, trastuzumab plus pertuzumab arm
most frequent serious event on this arm

notes: The cleanest published IHC-tier gradient in a pan-tumor HER2 cohort: 41% at 3+ falling to 8.3% at 1+ and zero at IHC 0, which is the quantitative form of the predictive-certainty problem the pending re-stain creates. Per-term AE rates come from the ClinicalTrials.gov Adverse Events tab for NCT02091141 (trastuzumab plus pertuzumab arm, 357 at risk), since the JCO Clinical Trial Update carries only a narrative safety statement.

intervention_dose: trastuzumab-pkrb 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg with paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks for six cycles, then trastuzumab maintenance
indication: HER2-positive recurrent or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
population_detail: HER2 positivity by IHC per 2013 ASCO/CAP breast criteria; 26 of 27 enrolled patients were evaluable.
safety_summary: Peripheral neuropathy in 88.9% at any grade, driven by the paclitaxel backbone; grade 3/4 events were mainly neutropenia 25.9%, thrombocytopenia 7.4% and anemia 7.4%.
notes: A payload-free HER2 antibody paired with a taxane reached 48% response in HER2-positive urothelial carcinoma, but the taxane is what makes it unusable here: neuropathy of any grade hit 88.9% and this patient already carries chronic CIPN. An erratum was published in ESMO Open 2024 (10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103708).

intervention_dose: 1.25 mg/kg IV on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle
indication: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma after platinum-containing chemotherapy and progression on PD-1/PD-L1 inhibition
population_detail: Prior platinum was required; this patient never received platinum, so the trial population is one line to the left of his course.
safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 51.4% versus 49.8% with chemotherapy. Peripheral neuropathy, skin reactions and hyperglycaemia are the class effects that drive dose modification.
notes: Establishes Nectin-4 as a survival-relevant target in urothelial carcinoma, in a post-platinum population this patient does not belong to. Per-term neuropathy and skin-toxicity rates sit in the paper's supplementary tables rather than the abstract; the abstract-level union rates are what is captured here.

intervention_dose: enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8 with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1, every 3 weeks
indication: Previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
population_detail: Cisplatin-eligible and cisplatin-ineligible patients both enrolled; co-primary endpoints PFS by BICR and OS.
safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 55.9% versus 69.5% with chemotherapy; median 12 cycles delivered, with peripheral neuropathy the usual reason for dose reduction over a long treatment course.
notes: This is the regimen that produced the patient's 25-month complete response, so it anchors what Nectin-4 targeting already achieved for him and sets the bar any re-targeting option is measured against. Per-term neuropathy rates are in the supplement, not the abstract.

intervention_dose: enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8 with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1, every 3 weeks
indication: Previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
population_detail: Overall EV-302 population with one additional year of follow-up beyond the primary analysis.
design: Updated analysis of a randomized phase 3 trial (EV-302, NCT04223856)
safety_summary: Peripheral sensory neuropathy was recorded in 228 of 440 patients (51.8%) on the enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab arm against 44 of 433 (10.2%) on chemotherapy, and maculopapular rash in 143 (32.5%) against 15 (3.5%). Serious pneumonitis (2.0%) and interstitial lung disease (0.9%) occurred only on the combination arm.

toxicities.notes: non-serious AE tab; 44/433 (10.2%) in the chemotherapy arm
non-serious AE tab; a further 7 serious (1.6%); 15/433 (3.5%) in the chemotherapy arm
non-serious; 6 serious (1.4%); 11/433 (2.5%) in the chemotherapy arm
serious AE tab; none in the chemotherapy arm
serious AE tab, term interstitial lung disease; none in the chemotherapy arm
serious AE tab, pancreatitis plus acute pancreatitis; lipase increase 1 (0.2%)

notes: Longer follow-up on the regimen this patient responded to, useful for judging what the 25-month complete response predicts about disease behaviour after stopping. Per-term AE rates come from the ClinicalTrials.gov Adverse Events tab for NCT04223856, which the update itself does not reproduce; the 51.8% sensory-neuropathy rate is the number that explains why this patient stopped at 25 months.

intervention_dose: enfortumab vedotin 1.25 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8 with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1, every 3 weeks
indication: Cisplatin-ineligible, previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
population_detail: 84.4% visceral disease; 55.6% with creatinine clearance <60 mL/min. Median follow-up 62.1 months.
design: Phase 1b/2 dose escalation and cohort A (EV-103/KEYNOTE-869, NCT03288545)
safety_summary: Peripheral sensory neuropathy 55.6% and fatigue 51.1% led the any-grade treatment-related events; grade >=3 events were led by lipase increase 17.8%, fatigue 11.1% and maculopapular rash 11.1%. Treatment-related AEs forced dose reduction in 33.3% and discontinuation in 44.4%, with one treatment-related death.

toxicities.notes: grade >=3 in 22.2%; median onset 0.7 months, median resolution 1.2 months
multiple organ dysfunction syndrome with concurrent bullous dermatitis

notes: The longest published follow-up on EV plus pembrolizumab, with 41.5% alive at five years, which is the reference class for a patient who reached complete response and then stopped for neuropathy. Per-term AE rates come from PMC full text (PMC13213747) because the abstract gives none and ClinicalTrials.gov posts no results for NCT03288545. Grade >=3 lipase increase at 17.8% is worth weighing against this patient's 2025 pancreatitis.

intervention_label: enfortumab vedotin rechallenge after toxicity interruption
intervention_dose: enfortumab vedotin resumed after interruption, with and without dose reduction
indication: Metastatic urothelial carcinoma treated at a single institution, January 2022 to December 2024
population_detail: 48 patients treated with enfortumab vedotin; 36 developed dermatologic adverse events and 20 resumed the drug after interrupting for them.
outcome: recurrence of dermatologic adverse events after rechallenge

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: dermatologic AEs on initial exposure (36/48), median onset 11 days

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: recurrence after rechallenge (13/20), generally lower grade than the first episode

safety_summary: Skin toxicity recurred in 13 of 20 rechallenged patients but was usually milder than the first episode; onset within seven days predicted progression to grade >=3.

toxicities.notes: median onset 11 days from first dose
recurrences generally lower grade than the initial event

notes: The only published cohort addressing enfortumab vedotin rechallenge, and it addresses skin toxicity rather than efficacy or neuropathy. Nothing here speaks to whether re-exposure works after a 25-month response, and neuropathy, the toxicity that stopped this patient, is not the toxicity studied.

intervention_dose: 10 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles
indication: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma after platinum-based chemotherapy and a checkpoint inhibitor
population_detail: Median three prior therapies; 66.4% visceral metastases. Entry required prior platinum, which this patient has not had.
design: Single-arm cohort 1 of a multicohort phase 2 registrational study (TROPHY-U-01, NCT03547973)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: central review; 77% had some decrease in measurable disease

safety_summary: Neutropenia dominated: grade >=3 neutropenia 35% and febrile neutropenia 10%; grade >=3 diarrhoea 10%.
notes: The cohort that produced the US accelerated approval later withdrawn in October 2024 after TROPiCS-04. Entry required prior platinum, so this patient would not have qualified, and the diarrhoea signal interacts with his current gastrointestinal intolerance.

intervention_dose: 10 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles
indication: Locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with progression after a checkpoint inhibitor, in patients cisplatin-ineligible at study entry
population_detail: Median age 72.5; 66% visceral metastases (29% liver); half had received platinum only in the perioperative setting.
design: Single-arm cohort 2 of a multicohort phase 2 study (TROPHY-U-01, NCT03547973)
safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-emergent AEs in 87%, most often neutropenia 34%, anemia 24%, leukopenia 19%, fatigue 18% and diarrhoea 16%.
notes: The one published urothelial cohort written for patients who never had cisplatin and progressed after checkpoint therapy, which is close to this patient's actual position. Thirty-eight patients, no randomisation, and 87% grade >=3 toxicity in a population older and frailer than this one.

intervention_label: sacituzumab govitecan versus taxane or vinflunine
intervention_dose: 10 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles
indication: Advanced urothelial carcinoma after platinum-based chemotherapy and checkpoint inhibitor therapy
population_detail: Confirmatory trial for the accelerated approval; median follow-up 9.2 months.
comparator: physician's choice paclitaxel, docetaxel or vinflunine

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: 9.0 mo with physician's choice; primary endpoint not met

safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs 67% versus 35%, and grade 5 treatment-emergent events 7% versus 2%; 16 of 25 fatal events were infections with neutropenia, mostly early in treatment. Primary prophylactic G-CSF was used in only 21%.

toxicities.notes: 16 of 25 were infections with neutropenia; 2% in the comparator arm

notes: The negative confirmatory trial behind the October 2024 withdrawal of the urothelial accelerated approval; response rate was higher with sacituzumab govitecan but survival was not. Early neutropenic infection deaths are the mechanism the authors propose for the disconnect, which is a dosing and prophylaxis problem rather than a target problem.

intervention_label: sacituzumab govitecan — TROP2 expression versus efficacy
intervention_dose: 10 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 of 21-day cycles
indication: Unresectable locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
population_detail: Archival tumor from TROPHY-U-01 cohorts 1-3; 146 of 192 treated patients had evaluable TROP2 data scored by H-score (0-300) and percentage membrane-positive tumor cells.
design: Prespecified biomarker analysis within a phase 2 study (TROPHY-U-01, NCT03547973)
outcome: association of TROP2 expression with ORR, PFS and OS
effect_size: no association: benefit observed across all expression levels

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: median tumor TROP2 H-score; median 91% membrane-positive cells (IQR 80-98)

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: proportion of patients with TROP2 expression at any level

safety_summary: Biomarker analysis; safety is reported in the parent cohort publications.
notes: The direct answer to the low-positive TROP2 question: response, PFS and OS were seen across expression levels, so a weak stain does not foreclose a TROP2 ADC. Two limits matter here: 98% of the trial population expressed TROP2 and the median H-score was 215, so the low end of the distribution is thinly represented and this patient's weak multiplex signal sits below almost everyone studied. No toxicities are recorded because the analysis reports no safety data of its own; the AE profile sits in the TROPHY-U-01 cohort rows and ClinicalTrials.gov posts no results for NCT03547973.

intervention_dose: sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 and 8 with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1, 21-day cycles
indication: Metastatic urothelial carcinoma progressing after platinum-based chemotherapy, in checkpoint-inhibitor-naive patients
population_detail: Checkpoint-naive by design; median age 67, 78% visceral metastases (29% liver). This patient is checkpoint-experienced, which is the mismatch.
design: Single-arm cohort 3 of a multicohort phase 2 study (TROPHY-U-01, NCT03547973)
safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs in 61%, most often neutropenia 37%, leukopenia 20% and diarrhoea 20%.
notes: Adding PD-1 blockade to a TROP2 ADC nearly doubled the single-agent response rate, but only in checkpoint-naive patients, and this patient progressed on pembrolizumab maintenance. Useful mainly as the ceiling estimate for ADC plus checkpoint combinations rather than as a transferable number.

intervention_label: gavocabtagene autoleucel (gavo-cel, mesothelin-directed TCR fusion construct T cells)
intervention_dose: 1 x 10^8 cells/m2 after lymphodepletion (RP2D)
indication: Treatment-refractory mesothelin-expressing solid tumors (mesothelioma, ovarian, cholangiocarcinoma)
population_detail: 32 patients dosed, 29 after lymphodepletion; 30 evaluable for response. Urothelial carcinoma was not among the enrolled histologies.
design: Phase 1 dose escalation within an ongoing phase 1/2 trial (NCT03907852)
safety_summary: Dose-limiting grade 3 pneumonitis and a fatal grade 5 bronchioalveolar haemorrhage occurred during escalation; grade >=3 pneumonitis 16% overall and none at the recommended dose, grade >=3 cytokine release syndrome 25% overall and 15% at the recommended dose.

toxicities.notes: none at the recommended phase 2 dose
dose-limiting toxicity during escalation; reported as a single event, not as a rate

notes: The strongest clinical activity signal for mesothelin-directed cell therapy so far, and the authors call the therapeutic window narrow. Pulmonary toxicity is the dose-limiting event, which matters given the unresolved chest CT question in this case.

intervention_label: huCART-meso (fully human anti-mesothelin CAR T cells)
intervention_dose: 1-3 x 10^7 CAR+ cells/m2, intravenous, intrapleural and/or intraperitoneal, with or without lymphodepletion
indication: Mesothelin-expressing lung adenocarcinoma, ovarian cancer and mesothelioma
population_detail: 14 ovarian, 5 mesothelioma, 1 lung adenocarcinoma. No urothelial patients.

outcomes.name: DCR
outcomes.notes: stable disease in 12 of 20; no objective responses

safety_summary: Cytokine release syndrome was the most common serious adverse event at 35%; CAR T cells persisted to 12 months in five patients and beyond two years in one.
notes: No objective responses in 20 patients, which is the realistic prior for conventional mesothelin CAR-T in solid tumors regardless of how strong the stain is. Sets the expectation for the mesothelin branch: a validated stain would open trial access, not predict benefit.

intervention_dose: 6.5 mg/kg IV on day 1 of each 21-day cycle
indication: Unresectable locally advanced or metastatic malignant pleural mesothelioma overexpressing mesothelin, after first-line platinum-pemetrexed
population_detail: Prospective screening for mesothelin overexpression, defined as 2+ or 3+ membrane staining in >=30% of viable tumor cells; 248 of 589 screened patients were randomized.
outcome: median progression-free survival by blinded central review
safety_summary: Grade >=3 events were less frequent than with vinorelbine for neutropenia (1% vs 39%) but ten treatment-emergent deaths occurred on anetumab ravtansine, three from pneumonia.

toxicities.notes: pneumonia n=3, dyspnoea n=2, sepsis n=2, other n=3

notes: A prospectively mesothelin-selected randomized trial that failed to beat vinorelbine, which is the most important negative result for the mesothelin-ADC concept. Selection on a validated 2+/3+ IHC threshold did not rescue it, so a strong stain alone is not a benefit argument.

intervention_label: gatipotuzumab (anti-TA-MUC1 antibody) plus an anti-EGFR antibody
intervention_dose: gatipotuzumab 1400 mg IV every 2 weeks with tomuzotuximab 1200 mg IV every 2 weeks
indication: Refractory EGFR-positive metastatic solid tumors, then an expansion in colorectal, non-small-cell lung, head and neck and breast cancer
population_detail: 20 patients in the primary phase and 32 in the expansion phase. Soluble TA-MUC1 was tracked in serum as a candidate companion biomarker.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: five RECIST partial responses (one primary phase, four expansion), all in colorectal cancer; percentage derived from the reported counts

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.effect_size: above-median baseline soluble TA-MUC1 associated with longer PFS and OS

safety_summary: No dose-limiting toxicity, no related serious adverse event and no related death across the whole study.
notes: Shows what MUC1 targeting has achieved clinically: safe, with responses confined to colorectal cancer and no urothelial data. It also makes the glycoform point concretely, since the antibody binds the tumor-associated MUC1 epitope rather than MUC1 protein as a multiplex panel would report it. An erratum was published in ESMO Open 2022 (10.1016/j.esmoop.2022.100549).

intervention_dose: up to 1 x 10^11 viral particles, subcutaneous
indication: Advanced adenocarcinoma (breast, lung, ovary)
population_detail: 21 patients with advanced adenocarcinomas; the trial was not designed to determine clinical efficacy.

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: injection-site reactions, the most common drug-related event

safety_summary: No dose-limiting toxicity at the maximal dose; all drug-related events were low grade, most commonly injection-site reactions in 15 of 21 patients.
notes: A safety-and-immunome study with no efficacy claim, included because it is one of the few completed MUC1-directed clinical trials with a published dataset. It sets the honest ceiling for the MUC1 branch in this case: no response evidence in any tumor type relevant here.

intervention_dose: single infusion after lymphodepletion, dose per escalation cohort
indication: PRAME-positive recurrent or refractory solid tumors in HLA-A*02-positive patients, including melanoma and sarcoma
population_detail: 27 patients in phase 1a escalation and 13 in phase 1b extension; 41 started lymphodepletion, 40 received IMA203. PRAME expression was measured by the sponsor's own RT-qPCR assay.
design: First-in-human open-label 3+3 phase 1 dose escalation and extension (ACTengine, NCT03686124)

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.effect_size: deep responses enriched at higher PRAME expression
outcomes.notes: exploratory; higher T-cell infiltration associated with longer PFS

safety_summary: Severe cytokine release syndrome in 4.9% and no severe neurotoxicity; the maximum tolerated dose was not reached.
notes: The best published clinical evidence for the PRAME/HLA-A*02:01 axis, and the response-versus-expression finding is what makes the pending PRAME result decision-relevant rather than merely eligibility-relevant. Responses were concentrated in melanoma and sarcoma; no urothelial patients were reported. An erratum was published in Nat Med 2025 (10.1038/s41591-025-03731-6).

intervention_label: PGV001 personalized neoantigen peptide vaccine plus atezolizumab
intervention_dose: PGV001 personalized long-peptide vaccine with poly-ICLC, given with atezolizumab
indication: Urothelial cancer, adjuvant and metastatic settings
population_detail: 12 enrolled; vaccine successfully manufactured for 10 (median 20.3 weeks). Four treated in the adjuvant setting, five in the metastatic setting with measurable disease.
outcome: feasibility, safety and vaccine-induced neoantigen-specific T-cell immunity
effect_size: on-treatment neoantigen-specific T-cell responses in all treated participants

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: all treated participants developed on-treatment neoantigen-specific T-cell responses

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: two of five achieved an objective response

outcomes.name: RFS
outcomes.notes: three of four recurrence-free at 39-month median follow-up

outcomes.name: TTNT
outcomes.notes: median vaccine manufacturing time from tissue to first dose

safety_summary: Most common treatment-related events were grade 1 injection-site reactions, fatigue and fever; all participants who started treatment completed the priming cycle.
notes: The only published personalized neoantigen vaccine trial in urothelial cancer, and the closest published analogue to what this patient is already receiving. Twelve patients, no control arm, and per-term AE percentages are not given in the abstract or the Nature Cancer summary; grade-1 terms are recorded without rates rather than dropped.

intervention_dose: intismeran 1 mg intramuscularly every 3 weeks for nine doses with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for 18 doses
indication: Resected stage IIIB-IV cutaneous melanoma
population_detail: 157 randomized 2:1 to combination versus pembrolizumab alone; median planned follow-up 60.3 months at the December 2025 cutoff.
outcome: recurrence-free survival hazard ratio at 5 years
median_dor_or_pfs: descriptive 5-year analysis; medians not reported in the abstract

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.effect_size: increased TCR clonality and novel clonotypes versus pembrolizumab alone
outcomes.notes: greater novel-clone expansion in patients without recurrence

safety_summary: No new safety signals at five years; per-term rates are not reported in this descriptive update.
notes: The most durable randomized signal that adding an individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccine to PD-1 blockade changes outcome, in resected melanoma rather than metastatic urothelial carcinoma. Empty toxicities are a source limit checked three ways: the 5-year update gives a one-sentence safety statement, the paper has no PMC record, and ClinicalTrials.gov posts no results for NCT03897881. The per-term table sits in the 2024 Lancet primary report.

intervention_label: autogene cevumeran (individualized uridine mRNA-lipoplex neoantigen vaccine) with atezolizumab and mFOLFIRINOX
intervention_dose: up to 20 neoantigens per patient, intravenous mRNA-lipoplex, after atezolizumab and before mFOLFIRINOX
indication: Resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, adjuvant setting
population_detail: 16 patients received atezolizumab and vaccine; 15 went on to mFOLFIRINOX. Vaccines were manufactured in real time from the surgical specimen.
outcome: vaccine-induced neoantigen-specific T-cell responses and recurrence-free survival by immune response
median_dor_or_pfs: mRFS not reached in immune responders vs 13.4 mo in non-responders

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: de novo high-magnitude neoantigen-specific T cells in 8 of 16; half targeted more than one vaccine neoantigen

safety_summary: One of 16 vaccinated patients had a grade 3 adverse event (fever and hypertension); all 16 had grade 1-2 events, and none of the 19 atezolizumab-treated patients had a grade 3 or higher event.

toxicities.term: any AE attributable to the vaccine
toxicities.notes: fever and hypertension in one patient; study safety threshold was 25%

toxicities.term: any AE attributable to the vaccine

notes: The template for reading this patient's EliSpot data: immunological response, not vaccination itself, tracked with outcome, and only half of vaccinated patients mounted one. His 2 of 14 evaluable pools with CD4-skewed reactivity sits at the weak end of that distribution. Grade-level AE data come from PMC full text (PMC10171177); no results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov and the paper reports attribution by drug rather than per CTCAE term.

intervention_label: neoantigen-selected tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, with and without pembrolizumab
intervention_dose: single TIL infusion after non-myeloablative lymphodepletion, followed by high-dose interleukin-2
indication: Treatment-refractory mismatch-repair-proficient metastatic gastrointestinal cancers
population_detail: Three sequential cohorts: 18 patients received bulk unselected TIL, 39 received neoantigen-selected TIL, 34 received neoantigen-selected TIL plus pembrolizumab.
design: Evolving single-arm phase 2 (NCT01174121, NCI Surgery Branch)
comparator: bulk unselected TIL (earlier cohort of the same trial)
outcome: objective response rate with neoantigen-selected TIL plus pembrolizumab

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.effect_size: response associated with more targeted neoantigens and more infused CD4+ neoantigen-reactive TILs

safety_summary: All patients had transient severe haematologic toxicity from lymphodepleting chemotherapy and seven (10%) required critical care support.
notes: This is NCT01174121, the same protocol the trial screener flagged as the neoantigen-TIL route, so the published readout is the direct efficacy prior for that option. Selecting for neoantigen reactivity lifted response from zero to 7.7%, and adding pembrolizumab to 23.5%, at the cost of universal severe cytopenias and a 10% critical-care rate. An erratum was published in Nat Med 2025 (10.1038/s41591-025-03708-5).

intervention_label: pembrolizumab in tissue TMB-high solid tumors
intervention_dose: 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles
indication: Previously treated advanced anal, biliary, cervical, endometrial, mesothelioma, neuroendocrine, salivary, small-cell lung, thyroid and vulvar cancers
population_detail: 790 patients evaluable for TMB; 102 (13%) had tTMB >=10 mut/Mb measured on FoundationOne CDx. Urothelial carcinoma was not one of the ten enrolled cohorts.
design: Prospective biomarker analysis within a multi-cohort phase 2 study (KEYNOTE-158, NCT02628067)
outcome: objective response rate in the tTMB-high group

outcomes.name: TRAE_rate
outcomes.notes: grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs in the tTMB-high safety set

safety_summary: Grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs in 15% of the 105 TMB-high patients; colitis was the only such event affecting more than one patient, and one fatal pneumonia was judged treatment related.
notes: The registration evidence behind the tumor-agnostic TMB-high pembrolizumab indication, and the reason the >=10 mut/Mb cutoff exists. Two problems apply here: the threshold was validated on FoundationOne CDx rather than the institutional 468-gene panel that produced this patient's 12.4 mut/Mb, and he has already progressed on prolonged pembrolizumab.

intervention_label: tumor mutational burden as a checkpoint-inhibitor biomarker, real-world cohort
intervention_dose: single-agent anti-PD-(L)1 per standard of care
indication: 24 advanced cancer types treated with single-agent checkpoint inhibition
population_detail: 8440 patients from a clinico-genomic database drawn from about 280 US treatment facilities, TMB measured by the FDA-approved companion-diagnostic algorithm.
design: Retrospective real-world cohort with validated mortality endpoint
outcome: real-world overall survival by TMB level
safety_summary: Observational survival analysis; no safety data collected.
notes: Puts this patient's 12.4 mut/Mb in the 10 to <20 band, where the adjusted survival advantage is real but modest, well short of the >=20 band. Retrospective, confounded by treatment selection, and no toxicity data by design. An erratum was published in J Immunother Cancer 2025 (10.1136/jitc-2024-010311corr1).

intervention_label: nivolumab induction with high-dose ipilimumab boost
intervention_dose: nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks x4, then for non-responders nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for two to four doses
indication: Metastatic or unresectable urothelial cancer of the bladder, urethra, ureter or renal pelvis after platinum-based chemotherapy
population_detail: 83 patients, Karnofsky >=70, measurable disease; 50 (60%) received at least one ipilimumab boost, given either for early non-response or for later progression on nivolumab maintenance.
comparator: historical nivolumab monotherapy response rate from CheckMate 275
safety_summary: Immune-mediated enterocolitis was the dominant severe toxicity at 11% grade 3-4, with diarrhoea in a further 6%; two treatment-related deaths, both from immune-mediated enterocolitis.
notes: The registered trial of exactly the manoeuvre the care team is considering, adding high-dose ipilimumab after PD-1 failure in urothelial carcinoma, and it produced responses in patients who had already failed nivolumab. Two treatment-related deaths from enterocolitis in 83 patients is the number to weigh against this patient's 2025 checkpoint-associated pancreatitis; entry also required prior platinum.

intervention_dose: nivolumab 1 mg/kg with ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks x4, then nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks
indication: Platinum-pretreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma
population_detail: Three cohorts compared: nivolumab 3 mg/kg alone (n=78), nivolumab 3 plus ipilimumab 1 (n=104), nivolumab 1 plus ipilimumab 3 (n=92). Patients were checkpoint-naive at entry.
comparator: nivolumab monotherapy and the lower-ipilimumab-dose cohort within the same study
outcome: investigator-assessed ORR, nivolumab 1 plus ipilimumab 3 cohort
median_dor_or_pfs: median DOR exceeded 22 months in all three arms

outcomes.name: DoR
outcomes.notes: median exceeded 22 months in every arm

outcomes.name: TRAE_rate
outcomes.notes: grade 3-4; 30.8% and 26.9% in the other arms

safety_summary: Grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs rose with ipilimumab dose, from 26.9% with nivolumab alone to 39.1% with nivolumab 1 plus ipilimumab 3; one grade 5 treatment-related pneumonitis occurred in each of the other two arms.

toxicities.notes: one each in the nivolumab and nivolumab 3 plus ipilimumab 1 arms

notes: Establishes the dose dependence of the CTLA-4 contribution in urothelial carcinoma: response climbed with ipilimumab dose and so did grade 3-4 toxicity. Patients here were checkpoint-naive, so it estimates the value of adding ipilimumab up front rather than after PD-1 failure. An erratum was published in J Clin Oncol 2019 (10.1200/JCO.19.01700).

population_detail: Selection required high FAP expression, defined as 68Ga-FAPI-46 PET SUVmax >=10 in more than 50% of all lesions.

intervention_label: ceralasertib (ATR inhibitor) monotherapy in ARID1A-deficient tumors
intervention_dose: 160 mg orally twice daily on days 1-14 of each 28-day cycle
indication: Locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors with ARID1A loss by immunohistochemistry
population_detail: 29 efficacy-evaluable patients, all with radiographic progression at entry and ARID1A loss confirmed by IHC rather than by sequencing alone. 13 had gynecologic malignancies.
median_dor_or_pfs: mDOR 33.7 mo in the responding gynecologic subset

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: four confirmed responses, three of them complete

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.subgroup: endometrioid endometrial or ovarian clear-cell carcinoma
outcomes.notes: all four responses came from this subset

outcomes.name: DCR
outcomes.notes: includes one uterine carcinosarcoma with stable disease

safety_summary: Safety detail is in the full text rather than the abstract; ceralasertib monotherapy toxicity is dominated by reversible myelosuppression at this schedule.
notes: The only prospective trial that selected patients on ARID1A loss, so it is the ceiling estimate for the ARID1A synthetic-lethality argument in this case, and every response came from gynecologic histology. Toxicities are empty after checking all three sources: the abstract carries no per-term AE data, the paper has no PMC record, and ClinicalTrials.gov posts no results for NCT03682289. Backfill from the Clin Cancer Res safety table when the full text is reachable.

intervention_label: berzosertib (M6620/VX-970, ATR inhibitor) alone and with carboplatin
intervention_dose: 240 mg/m2 IV once or twice weekly as monotherapy; 90 mg/m2 with carboplatin AUC5 in combination
indication: Advanced solid tumors, unselected for ARID1A
population_detail: 17 patients received monotherapy and 23 the carboplatin combination. Molecular annotation was retrospective rather than an entry criterion.
outcome: antitumor activity and recommended phase 2 dose
effect_size: one durable complete response (ATM loss plus ARID1A mutation), one partial response, 15 with stable disease
median_dor_or_pfs: PFS 29 months in the complete responder at last assessment

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: one metastatic colorectal cancer with ATM loss and an ARID1A mutation; PFS 29 months

outcomes.name: DCR
outcomes.notes: one complete response, one partial response, 15 stable disease; percentage derived from the reported counts

safety_summary: Monotherapy was well tolerated with no dose-limiting toxicity; the carboplatin combination produced mechanism-based haematologic toxicity requiring dose delays and reductions at higher doses.

toxicities.notes: described as mechanism-based and dose-limiting at higher doses; per-term rates in the full text, not the abstract

notes: The single durable complete response in this first-in-class study occurred in a tumor carrying both ATM loss and an ARID1A mutation, which is the anecdote the ARID1A-ATR hypothesis is usually built on. One patient in an unselected phase 1 is not a benefit estimate, and ARID1A alone was never the selection criterion.

exclusion_reason: Subgroup report of the endometrial, cervical and ovarian cohorts of the same trial; the bladder-cohort estimand this case needs is in the primary publication.
notes: Read to check whether the exploratory biomarker analyses generalised to the bladder cohort. They are gynecology-specific.

intervention_label: trastuzumab deruxtecan — DESTINY-PanTumor02 biliary and pancreatic subgroup
exclusion_reason: Subgroup report covering the biliary tract and pancreatic cohorts, neither of which informs the bladder cohort estimand.
Same cohort as the EV-301 primary publication already included; longer follow-up does not change the post-platinum population mismatch that limits its relevance here.
Perioperative muscle-invasive bladder cancer; wrong setting for a patient with treated metastatic disease and prior prolonged enfortumab vedotin exposure.
Preclinical work in human cancer models and directed at R248Q rather than R175H; the researcher agent owns preclinical evidence.
notes: Searched deliberately for clinical readouts on the TP53 R175H/HLA-A*02:01 axis and found none: CLSP-1025 (NCT06778863) and NT-175 (NCT05877599) have no published results. The axis is trial-access-only at present.
